sourceChecks.text: David said to him, “How did it go? Please tell me.” He answered, “The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead. Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:4で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:5で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:12で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:17で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan’s bow didn’t turn back. Saul’s sword didn’t return empty.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:22で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives. In their death, they were not divided. They were swifter than eagles. They were stronger than lions.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:23で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: How the mighty have fallen in the middle of the battle! Jonathan was slain on your high places.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:25で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You have been very pleasant to me. Your love to me was wonderful, surpassing the love of women.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA1:26で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news came about Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse picked him up and fled. As she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA4:4で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA9:1で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: The king said, “Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may show the kindness of God to him?” Ziba said to the king, “Jonathan still has a son, who is lame in his feet.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA9:3で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, fell on his face, and showed respect. David said, “Mephibosheth?” He answered, “Behold, your servant!”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA9:6で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA9:7で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: But the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA21:7で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: So David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hanged them in the day that the Philistines killed Saul in Gilboa;
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA21:12で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: and he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son. They also gathered the bones of those who were hanged.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA21:13で本文がヨナタンを名指す。

sourceChecks.text: They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father; and they performed all that the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer for the land.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 2SA21:14で本文がヨナタンを名指す。
